title: Lift a skimmer basket out of its well by its folded handle
instruction: Take the skimmer basket out and set it on the deck tray.
context: Pool technicians empty the skimmer basket on every visit. It sits in a close-fitting well below the deck, so the only hold is its handle, folded flat over the leaves; a tipped basket spills leaves back into the skimmer and blocks the pump suction. Done by: pool and spa service technicians. Unlike TK-ERQ59J (a flush cover lifted with separate keys) and TK-5KQLXV (latch a toolbox, then carry it by its handle), this task needs a folded handle raised inside a recess before the lift.
setup: Station table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x away from the robot, y to its left; heights above the table top. Pool deck (fixed, grey concrete-coloured block): 75 mm tall, covering x 17.0 to 37.0 and y -2.0 to 32.0, with a round skimmer well through it. Skimmer well (fixed, darker grey walls): a 12-sided bore 108 mm across its flats (112 mm across its corners), centred at (27.0, 22.0), 75 mm deep down to the table, which is its floor. Skimmer basket (loose, 0.30 kg): a white plastic cylinder 100 mm across and 45 mm tall, standing on the table in the middle of the well, so there is 4 mm of clearance to the wall all round and its rim is 30 mm below the deck surface. It is full of leaves (dark brown) level with its rim; basket and leaves are one rigid body. Handle (part of the basket, black wire, 20 g): a grip bar 10 mm across and 84 mm long along x, carried on two 4 mm legs 40 mm either side of the basket's centre, hinged on an axis along x through the basket's centre 5 mm above its rim; the grip bar's axis is 26 mm from the hinge axis. At the start the handle lies folded flat toward the robot's left over the leaves, the grip bar centred at (27.0, 24.6), its top 20 mm below the deck surface. It swings up freely to a stop 5 degrees past upright (toward the robot's right), where it stays standing. Deck tray (fixed, blue plastic, on the deck): inside 130 x 130 mm, centred at (27.0, 6.0); a 3 mm floor (floor surface 78 mm above the table) and a rim 5 mm thick standing 6 mm above the floor. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured with a ruler, a photo and the video. Pass/fail. 1.0 when the basket stands on the tray floor (the centre of its base within 1 mm of the floor), upright within 5 degrees, wholly inside the tray (its centre within 15 mm of the tray's centre along x and along y), and still for 1 s. The handle may be up or folded. 0 in every other case: the basket still in the well, held or hanging over the tray, propped on the tray rim, on the deck or the table, or still moving. 0 for the whole trial if the basket ever tips more than 45 degrees from upright (its leaves spill), even if it is set upright on the tray afterwards.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the basket back in the middle of the well and fold the handle flat toward the robot's left.
fidelity: Approximate, about 0.6 times real size (real baskets are often 160 to 180 mm across). The skimmer's deck lid is off before the trial. Basket and leaves are one rigid cylinder with a flat top, so it cannot be gripped from inside; a real basket is open mesh holding wet leaves. The well is a 12-sided bore. The handle is one rigid bail on a free hinge with a stop just past upright. Friction is the simulator's (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), not measured.
